title: How AI is Transforming Student Learning at MVHS
excerpt: We explore how artificial intelligence tools are being integrated into classrooms, the benefits we've observed, and the challenges we're working to address. This article shares real experiences from students and teachers using AI-powered study platforms.
author: Sarah Chen
content:
The AI Evolution in MVHS Classrooms

Artificial Intelligence is no longer a futuristic concept; it is an active, evolving tool within the MVHS learning environment. We are focused on integrating AI ethically and effectively, moving beyond simple novelty to genuine educational enhancement. Our approach centers on accelerating student mastery of foundational concepts, freeing up human instructors to focus on creativity, critical thinking, and personalized mentorship. AI tools are currently used across subjects from personalized math practice to generating instant feedback on introductory coding assignments.

Personalized Learning Pathways

One of the most profound benefits we've observed is the ability of AI platforms to adapt content difficulty in real-time. Unlike traditional software, these tools can identify exactly where a student’s knowledge gap lies and offer highly specific remediation or advanced challenges. This ensures that every student is consistently learning in their optimal zone, maximizing efficiency. Teachers are leveraging data from these platforms to group students for targeted instruction, transforming the classroom into a responsive, student-centric space.

Addressing the Ethical Questions and Challenges

Integrating AI comes with significant responsibility. Our MVHS Tech Internship addresses challenges head-on, particularly concerns regarding data privacy and the potential for algorithmic bias. We host regular workshops for students and staff on responsible AI usage, emphasizing that these tools are complements to, not replacements for, human effort and original thought. Furthermore, a recent survey among our students revealed that approximately 25% still feel morally opposed to using AI in academic work, highlighting the need for continuous, open dialogue about boundaries and ethical guidelines.

The Future is Collaborative

The successful integration of AI requires collaboration among students, teachers, administrators, and the wider community. By making AI usage transparent and focusing on tools that enhance core learning objectives, we are preparing MVHS students not just to use future technology, but to shape it. We encourage everyone to join the conversation and explore these transformative tools with a mindset of curiosity and caution.

title: Building Community Through Tech Events
excerpt: How our AI Parent Night used technology events to engage students, parents, and staff while building community and understanding of AI in education.
author: Sean Lin
content:
The Planning Process

AI Parent Night was an event designed to help parents learn more about how artificial intelligence is being used in education, how it can support student learning, and how it affects our future careers. Our goal was to make the topic of AI easier to understand and show how it connects to what students are doing in class. The first step was coming up with a plan. A few weeks before the event on September 24th, our group met after school to discuss what we should include. We wanted to make sure that our parents’ questions could be resolved, so we sent out survey forms for students and staff input, as well as a survey for parents about what questions they wanted answered. We split into multiple groups: setup, communication and guest coordination. Everybody had their own role, which really helped us stay organized.

Contacting Guest Speakers

Finding guest speakers was one of the trickiest parts. We wanted to invite people who could connect both parents and students, clearing any misconceptions and questions in the way. After sending a few emails, we were thrilled when Ly Nguyen, Sandra McGonagle, Alex Levich, and our principal Kip Glazer agreed to join. We chose them because each brought a different perspective ranging from district level leadership to classroom experience and industry insight. We organized a panel discussion featuring them, where each speaker shared their unique perspective on education, technology, and school leadership. Their insights helped parents better understand how AI impacts both teaching and learning.

The Big Day

The day of the event was busy, but exciting. We arrived early to set up the space, check the microphones, practice the presentation, and welcome in our parents. In no time, all the seats were full of parents, eager to learn something new. We presented our findings, showing what was beneath the project we had worked hard on for weeks. Such as the types of AI tools that students use and the benefits and drawbacks of utilizing AI. Something that stood out to us was the fact that a quarter of the students that took the survey were morally opposed to using AI. As we spoke, we could see the parents’ interests grow. Some nodded along, others took notes and asked thoughtful questions.

After our presentation, we transitioned into our guest speaker panel. The guest speakers followed up with their own insights, connecting perfectly to our mission statement and goals. They discussed topics such as where we should draw the line between positive and harmful uses of AI, and what it takes to build a successful career in this new era of artificial intelligence. Then, we followed with our student speaker panel, giving parents a direct look at how AI affects students’ real experiences, challenges, and hopes. When the event wrapped up, there was a real sense of pride in the room. All our preparation had paid off, and it felt amazing to see just how engaged everybody was.

Reflections and Impact

Looking back, the AI Parent Event taught us a lot about teamwork, communication, and the effort it takes to bring an idea to something real. We learned how to manage deadlines and stay calm under pressure. But most importantly, we saw how an event like this can strengthen our school community and inspire more students and parents to get involved with future projects. Additionally, parents left with a sense of clarity about AI in education, and several even reached out afterward asking if we could host another session. With the amount of interest and support we received, we’re even considering holding a second event during the second semester.
